mainTopic: When a child of a forbidden union is פגום for כהונה or a ממזר: a remarried divorcée, unions forbidden under כרת, and an עבד or גוי with a Jewish woman.
overview: This amud discusses when a child born from a forbidden union is פגום, meaning unfit for כהונה, even if he is not a ממזר. First the גמרא says that 'all agree', even שמעון התימני, that the child of a man who remarries his divorcée after she married someone else is פגום. It learns this with a קל וחומר from an אלמנה married to a כהן גדול. Three objections are raised: a logical one (the widow herself becomes a חללה), the פסוק 'היא תועבה', and a ברייתא where חכמים call the child 'fit'. The גמרא answers the ברייתא and the פסוק, but the widow objection stands, so that version of the statement falls. The statement is then reworded: everyone, even רבי יהושע, agrees that a child from a union forbidden under כרת is פגום. Here the widow objection does not apply, because such a union makes the woman a זונה. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that everyone, even שמעון התימני, agrees that the child of an עבד or a גוי with a Jewish woman is a ממזר, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The child is flawed for the priesthood
steps.stepSummary: The end of the earlier statement: all agree that the child of this forbidden union is פגום לכהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...that the child is flawed for the priesthood.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of a ruling that began before this section: everyone agrees the child from this forbidden union is פגום for כהונה. The next lines will analyze this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being פגום is different from being a ממזר. A פגום child is not forbidden to marry into the general community. The flaw concerns the priesthood: a girl like this may not marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The child born from the union
Flawed in lineage; for a girl, unfit to marry a כהן
The priesthood

steps.confusionAlert: פגום does NOT mean ממזר. A ממזר is barred from marrying into the community at all. A פגום child is only flawed with respect to כהונה.

phrases.english: that the child is flawed for the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling stated just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees the child of this forbidden union is פגום לכהונה.

steps.title: Who is included in 'all agree'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the words 'all agree' are meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is 'all agree' coming to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. If the ruling says 'everyone agrees,' there must be someone we might have thought disagrees, so who is it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'all' suggests the ruling holds even for someone whose view would seem to lead elsewhere. The גמרא wants to name that person.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: Who is 'all agree' including?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view is the phrase 'all agree' meant to include?

steps.title: It includes שמעון התימני
steps.stepSummary: 'All' includes שמעון התימני. He holds that no ממזר comes from a לאו-level prohibition, but he agrees the child is still פגום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is שמעון התימני. Even though שמעון התימני said that a ממזר does not come from relations forbidden by a negative commandment, granted the child is not a ממזר, he is at least flawed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'all' includes שמעון התימני. He says this child is not a ממזר, but he still agrees the child is פגום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Remarrying one's divorcée after she married another is only a לאו, so שמעון התימני would say the child is not a ממזר. The ruling teaches that even he admits a lower-level flaw, פגום לכהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A child of certain forbidden unions, barred from marrying into the community
Relations forbidden by a negative commandment (a לאו)
Granted that
At least, in any case

phrases.english: It is Shimon HaTimni,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר שִׁמְעוֹן הַתִּימְנִי:
phrases.english: for even though Shimon HaTimni said:
there is no mamzer from those liable for negative prohibitions,
granted that he is not a mamzer,
he is at least flawed,

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְעוֹן הַתִּימְנִי דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר שִׁמְעוֹן הַתִּימְנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'All' includes שמעון התימני, who denies ממזרות here but agrees the child is פגום.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ממזר and פגום are separate levels of flaw. Someone can deny the first and still accept the second.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from a widow married to a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The source for פגום is a קל וחומר: the child of an אלמנה and a כהן גדול is פגום even though her prohibition applies only to him. So the child here, whose prohibition applies to everyone, should surely be פגום.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes through a קל וחומר from a widow. If a widow married to a כהן גדול, whose prohibition does not apply to everyone, has a flawed son, then this woman, whose prohibition applies to everyone, should all the more so have a flawed son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason the child is פגום by building a קל וחומר from the case of an אלמנה and a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow is forbidden only to a כהן גדול, a narrow prohibition, yet her child from him is still פגום. A divorcée who remarried is forbidden to her first husband, and that rule applies to every Jew. The broader prohibition looks stricter, so the child should be פגום all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A widow
The High Priest
Applies equally to everyone
Isn't it logical?

phrases.english: from an a fortiori inference from a widow.
Just as a widow married to a High Priest,
whose prohibition is not equal for all,
phrases.notes: Only a כהן גדול is forbidden to marry a widow. Everyone else may.

phrases.english: her son is flawed,
this woman, whose prohibition is equal for all,
phrases.notes: 'This woman' is the divorcée who married someone else. Every Jew is forbidden to take her back.

phrases.english: is it not logical that her son is flawed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for why שמעון התימני would agree the child is פגום.
steps.raayaObject: That the child of a remarried divorcée is פגום לכהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the child of an אלמנה and a כהן גדול

steps.title: The widow case is different: she herself becomes disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר can be refuted. The widow herself becomes a חללה through the forbidden union, which is not true of the remarried divorcée.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can be refuted: what about a widow? She herself becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר by pointing out something stricter about the widow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a widow lives with a כהן גדול, she herself becomes a חללה, disqualified from כהונה. Since her own status is damaged, it makes sense that her child is damaged too. The divorcée's status is not damaged in the same way, so we cannot learn from the widow.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be refuted
What about...? (pointing out a difference)
Becomes a חללה, disqualified from כהונה

steps.confusionAlert: This is a classic פירכא. The גמרא does not say the widow law is wrong. It shows the widow case has an extra stringency, so the comparison fails.

phrases.english: There is room to refute:
What about a widow?
She herself becomes disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 4.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The widow herself becomes a חללה, a stringency the remarried divorcée lacks.

steps.title: 'She is an abomination', not her children
steps.stepSummary: A second objection: the פסוק says 'היא תועבה', which implies only she is an abomination and her children are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it is written 'she is an abomination', but her children are not abominations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second objection, this time from a פסוק. The Torah stresses that 'she' is the abomination, which suggests the children are not flawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first objection only weakened the logic. This one brings a פסוק that seems to say the opposite, that the children have no flaw at all. That puts the ruling of 'all agree it is פגום' under real pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore
An abomination
It is written

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that the child is פגום now faces two objections: a logical one (the widow herself becomes a חללה) and one from the פסוק 'היא תועבה'. A third objection, from a ברייתא, comes next. Step 15 answers the פסוק objection; only the widow objection survives (step 16).

phrases.english: And furthermore, 'she is an abomination' is written,
but her children are not abominations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the קל וחומר, this time from a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that the child is פגום
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק limits the abomination to 'היא', the woman herself, which implies her children are not flawed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that 'all agree' the child is פגום לכהונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'היא' excludes the children, so the Torah itself seems to say they have no flaw.

steps.title: A third objection: a ברייתא where the child is called fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא and חכמים argue about a man who remarries his divorcée, marries his חלוצה, or marries a relative of his חלוצה. חכמים say she and her child are both fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, a ברייתא teaches: A man who remarries his divorcée, or marries his חלוצה, or marries a relative of his חלוצה: רבי עקיבא says his קידושין do not take effect, she does not need a גט from him, she is unfit, her child is unfit, and we force him to send her away. חכמים say his קידושין do take effect, she needs a גט from him, she is fit, and her child is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more reason to doubt that the child here is פגום, by quoting a ברייתא where חכמים call the child 'fit'. This step sets up the source, and the next step draws the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ועוד' (and furthermore) tells us this continues the attack on the קל וחומר from steps 5 and 6. According to חכמים, the remarried divorcée's child is כשר. If 'fit' means fit even for כהונה, then the child is not פגום at all, against what step 4 tried to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow released from יבום through the חליצה ceremony
A close relative of the woman he did חליצה with
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
We force him to divorce her

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the חלוצה cases. Our סוגיא only cares about the first case, the man who remarries his divorcée, and about the words 'her child is fit'.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who remarries his divorcée,
phrases.notes: This is our סוגיא's case: she married someone else in between, then came back to her first husband.

phrases.english: and one who marries his חלוצה,
and one who marries a relative of his חלוצה,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין לוֹ בָּהּ קִדּוּשִׁין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: his betrothal of her does not take effect,
and she does not need a bill of divorce from him,
and she is unfit, and her child is unfit,
and we force him to send her away.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּהּ קִדּוּשִׁין,
phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: his betrothal of her does take effect,
and she needs a bill of divorce from him,
and she is fit and her child is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third objection, after the two in steps 5 and 6, to the claim that the child is פגום.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion of the קל וחומר in step 4, that the remarried divorcée's child is פגום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא has חכמים calling this child 'fit', which seems to contradict the claim that he is פגום.

steps.title: Reading 'her child is fit' as fit for כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'her child is fit' must mean fit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fit for whom? Is it not fit for כהונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the ברייתא: when חכמים say the child is fit, they seem to mean fit for כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the child is fit for כהונה, he is not פגום, because being פגום means being unfit for כהונה. This would directly contradict the claim of step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: For whom? (to marry whom, or fit for what)
Is it not? (begins a suggested answer the גמרא thinks is obvious)
The priesthood; being fit to serve as, or marry, a כהן

phrases.english: For whom? Is it not for the priesthood?
phrases.notes: The question is about the words 'her child is fit' from חכמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the remarried divorcée's child is not פגום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: חכמים in the ברייתא: 'וּוְלָדָהּ כָּשֵׁר', read as fit for כהונה.

steps.title: No, the child is only called fit to marry into the קהל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: 'fit' about the child may mean only fit to marry into the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means fit for the קהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by giving 'fit' a smaller meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being fit for the קהל only means the child is not a ממזר. That fits with step 3, where even שמעון התימני agrees there is no ממזר here. The child could still be פגום for כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: The congregation of Israel; marrying into it means the person is not a ממזר

phrases.english: No, it means for the congregation of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'her child is fit' means fit for כהונה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Fit' could mean only fit to marry into the קהל, which says nothing about כהונה.

steps.title: Then 'she is fit' must also mean the קהל, which is too obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that 'she is fit' cannot mean fit for the קהל, because that is obvious. So it must mean fit for כהונה, and the child's fitness should mean the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, 'she is fit', fit for whom? If you say for the קהל, that is obvious. Would she become unfit for the קהל just because she had a forbidden relationship? Rather, it must mean for כהונה. And since for her it means כהונה, for her child it also means כהונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 9. It shows that 'she is fit' must be about כהונה, and then says the child's 'fit' in the same sentence should mean the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who has a forbidden relationship becomes at most a זונה, and a זונה is forbidden only to a כהן, never to the rest of the קהל. So saying she is fit for the קהל would teach nothing. Since 'she is fit' must mean fit for כהונה, the matching words 'her child is fit' should also mean fit for כהונה, which brings back the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if we accept your answer)
If you say (tries out a possibility in order to reject it)
It is obvious; why would it need to be taught?
She had a forbidden relationship (making her a זונה)
Since (introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just shown)

phrases.english: If so, 'she is fit', for whom?
If you say for the congregation, it is obvious!
Because she had a forbidden relationship, would she be unfit for the congregation?!
Rather, is it not for the priesthood?
And since 'she' means for the priesthood,
her child also means for the priesthood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9 and brings back the proof of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 9 that 'her child is fit' means only fit for the קהל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'She is fit' must mean fit for כהונה, since fitness for the קהל would be obvious. The two halves of one sentence should mean the same thing, so the child is fit for כהונה too.

steps.title: The two halves can be about different things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'she is fit' and 'her child is fit' do not have to mean the same thing; each is read in its own way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a proof? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 10: just because the two phrases sit next to each other doesn't mean they talk about the same kind of fitness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the mother, 'fit' means fit for כהונה, since anything else would be obvious. For the child, 'fit' can mean only fit for the קהל, meaning not a ממזר. So the ברייתא does not prove the child is fit for כהונה, and he can still be פגום.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? Are the cases really connected?
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is; each part has its own meaning

phrases.english: Are these comparable?
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the mother, fit for כהונה; 'that one' is the child, fit for the קהל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and protects the deflection of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the phrase: two neighboring words in one sentence are read with different meanings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'she is fit' means fit for כהונה, 'her child is fit' must mean the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each half has its own meaning: the mother is fit for כהונה, while the child is only said to be fit for the קהל.

steps.title: Support from רבי עקיבא's half of the same ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer: in רבי עקיבא's opinion, 'she is unfit' must also mean unfit for כהונה, so here too the mother and child are read differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also reasonable, since the first part teaches: She is unfit and her child is unfit. She is unfit for whom? If you say for the קהל, would she become unfit for the קהל just because she had a forbidden relationship? Rather, it must mean for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that its answer in step 11 makes sense by looking at רבי עקיבא's words in the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי עקיבא's half, 'she is unfit' can only mean unfit for כהונה, for the same reason as before: a זונה is still allowed to the קהל. But 'her child is unfit' in his half is about marrying into the קהל, since for רבי עקיבא a ממזר can come from a לאו (unlike שמעון התימני in step 3). So the same ברייתא already uses 'she' and 'her child' in different ways, which supports reading חכמים's half the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (support for the answer just given)
The first part of the ברייתא or משנה
Unfit (for marriage to a certain group)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove the child is fit for כהונה. In both halves, the mother's status is about כהונה while the child's status can be about the קהל, so the child can still be פגום.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since the first clause teaches:
She is unfit and her child is unfit.
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא's opinion from the start of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: She is unfit for whom?
If you say for the congregation,
because she had a forbidden relationship, would she be unfit for the congregation?!
Rather, is it not for the priesthood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 11 using the other half of the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That 'she' and 'her child' in the ברייתא can refer to different kinds of fitness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's clause 'הִיא פְּסוּלָה וּוְלָדָהּ פָּסוּל', where 'she is unfit' can only mean unfit for כהונה.

steps.title: In רבי עקיבא's case, the child is unfit even for the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that in רבי עקיבא's clause, 'her child is unfit' cannot mean only unfit for כהונה. רבי עקיבא holds the child is a ממזר, so it must mean unfit for the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And her child is unfit': unfit for what? If you say unfit for כהונה, that would mean he is fit for the קהל. But רבי עקיבא said the child is a ממזר! So it must obviously mean unfit for the קהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started in step 12. It shows that in רבי עקיבא's clause, the child's 'unfit' means something different from the mother's 'unfit'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 we saw that the mother's 'unfit' means unfit for כהונה. Now the גמרא shows the child's 'unfit' must mean unfit for the whole קהל, because רבי עקיבא calls such a child a ממזר. So in this one sentence, the same word means two different things for mother and child.

keyTerms.meaning: her child
unfit, disqualified
if you say
a child from a forbidden union, who may not marry into the Jewish people
it is obvious

phrases.english: And 'her child is unfit': unfit for what?
If you say unfit for the priesthood,
that would mean he is fit to marry into the congregation?
But didn't Rabbi Akiva say the child is a mamzer!
Rather, it is obvious: unfit for the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 12 by explaining the child's half of רבי עקיבא's clause.
steps.raayaObject: The claim from step 11 that 'she is ___' and 'her child is ___' can mean different things in the same sentence.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's clause: the mother's 'unfit' means unfit for כהונה, while the child's 'unfit' means unfit for the קהל, since he is a ממזר.

steps.title: Each half of the clause is read on its own terms
steps.stepSummary: Since the first clause reads mother and child differently, the latter clause can do the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since in the first clause this one is as it is and that one is as it is, in the latter clause too, this one is as it is and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the proof. It applies the lesson of the first clause to the latter clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw that in the first clause, the mother's 'unfit' and the child's 'unfit' mean different things. So there is no problem saying that in the latter clause, the mother's 'fit' and the child's 'fit' also mean different things. This removes the objection from step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: the first clause
the latter clause
this one is as it is and that one is as it is; each is read in its own way

steps.whatToRemember: In this source, the mother's status and the child's status do not have to be read the same way. So it does not prove that the child of a remarried divorcée is fit for כהונה.

phrases.english: And since in the first clause
phrases.notes: That is רבי עקיבא's clause, the one we just looked at.

phrases.english: this one is as it is and that one is as it is,
in the latter clause too,
this one is as it is and that one is as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in steps 12 and 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The objection from this source is answered: 'she is fit' and 'her child is fit' may mean different levels of fitness.

steps.title: 'She is an abomination' excludes her rival wife, not her children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier objection from the פסוק 'היא תועבה'. The word 'she' comes to exclude her צרה, so her children may still be disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'she is an abomination' can also be explained: she is an abomination, but her rival wife is not an abomination. But her children are abominations.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the objection from the source is settled, the גמרא answers another earlier objection, the one from the פסוק 'היא תועבה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the word 'היא' (she) seemed to mean that only she is an abomination, not her children. The גמרא now says 'she' comes to exclude her צרה instead. That leaves room for her children to be disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: an abomination
her rival wife, the other wife of the same husband
abominations, here meaning disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the פסוק says the children are definitely disqualified. The גמרא is only showing that the word 'she' does not have to exclude the children.

phrases.english: And 'she is an abomination' also,
phrases.notes: דברים 24:4. This is the objection from the פסוק that was raised before the discussion of the source.

phrases.english: she is an abomination,
but her rival wife is not an abomination,
but her children are abominations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the source discussion, the גמרא goes back to an earlier objection from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the word 'היא' comes to exclude.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'היא' (she) means only she is an abomination, not her children.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'היא' excludes her צרה, so her children may still be disqualified.

steps.title: The widow comparison remains a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the objection to the widow comparison is still unanswered. A widow becomes disqualified herself, which is not true here.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the widow is still a difficulty: what about a widow? She herself becomes disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says two objections were answered, but one still stands. The comparison to a widow does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof compared this case to a widow who marries a כהן גדול. But the widow herself becomes disqualified (מתחללת) through that union. The remarried divorcée does not become disqualified that way. So you cannot learn the child's status from the widow, and this objection is left unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow (here, one who marries a כהן גדול)
it remains a difficulty
becomes a חללה, disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: The objections from the source and from the פסוק were answered, but the widow objection still stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because this objection is not answered, the proof that the child of a remarried divorcée is disqualified does not hold up.

phrases.english: But the widow is a difficulty:
what about a widow,
since she herself becomes disqualified!
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the objection it raised earlier. The widow is hurt by the union herself, and the remarried divorcée is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering two objections, the גמרא admits that the third, the widow comparison, stands.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר comparing a remarried divorcée to a widow married to a כהן גדול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The widow becomes disqualified herself, so she is stricter. You cannot use her to prove something about a woman who does not become disqualified.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פירכא from the widow (she herself becomes a חללה) stands, so the original version of the statement about a remarried divorcée cannot be sustained. This leads to the rewording in step 17.

steps.title: The statement is reworded to be about unions forbidden under כרת
steps.stepSummary: Since the old version failed, the גמרא gives a new version of רב יוסף's statement: everyone agrees that a child from a union forbidden under כרת is פגום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this: רב יוסף said in the name of רבי שמעון ברבי: Everyone agrees that when a man has relations with a woman forbidden to him under כרת, the child is flawed.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier version of the statement could not stand, so the גמרא says it must have been said differently. It gives the new wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is now a union forbidden under כרת. That change lets the widow objection from Step 16 be answered (see Step 22). The ruling is that the child is פגום, meaning flawed for כהונה. It does not say the child is a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (the גמרא is rewording a statement)
Forbidden relations punished with כרת (being cut off)
Flawed in lineage; unfit for כהונה
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up פגום and ממזר. A פגום child is only unfit for כהונה. A ממזר may not marry into the קהל at all.

phrases.english: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, so this is his son.

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּבָא עַל חַיָּיבֵי כָּרֵיתוֹת
phrases.english: All agree about one who has relations with a woman forbidden under karet
that the child is flawed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier version that failed against the widow objection in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that a child from a union forbidden under כרת is פגום.

steps.title: Who is included in 'everyone agrees'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose agreement the words 'everyone agrees' are meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is meant by 'everyone agrees'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. 'Everyone agrees' suggests some sage might have disagreed, so who is that?
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Everyone agrees' usually points to a sage you might have thought disagrees. The גמרא wants to know which sage that is.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?

phrases.english: Who is meant by 'all agree'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the wording of the new statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sage is included by the phrase 'everyone agrees'.

steps.title: Even רבי יהושע agrees the child is flawed
steps.stepSummary: It is רבי יהושע. He holds there is no ממזר from חייבי כריתות, but he agrees the child is at least פגום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהושע. Even though רבי יהושע said there is no ממזר from unions forbidden under כרת, granted the child is not a ממזר, he is at least flawed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'everyone' is meant to include רבי יהושע. You might have thought he would say the child is fully fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that only a union punished by death by בית דין produces a ממזר, not a union punished by כרת. Even so, he agrees the child is not completely clean. The child is פגום, unfit for כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, even if
At least, in any case
A child of a forbidden union who may not marry into the קהל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: For even though Rabbi Yehoshua said:
there is no mamzer from unions forbidden under karet,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהושע's view in a משנה later in the מסכתא.

phrases.english: granted that he is not a mamzer,
he is at least flawed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ. דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Everyone' includes רבי יהושע. He denies the child is a ממזר but agrees the child is פגום.

steps.title: The source: a קל וחומר from a widow married to a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A widow is forbidden only to a כהן גדול, yet her child from him is flawed. A woman forbidden to everyone should surely have a flawed child too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is learned through a קל וחומר from a widow. A widow with a כהן גדול is forbidden only to him, not to everyone, yet her son is flawed. This woman is forbidden to everyone. Isn't it logical that her son is flawed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for why the child is פגום. It uses a קל וחומר (a 'how much more so' argument).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow's prohibition is weak: only a כהן גדול may not marry her. Still, her child from him is a חלל, which means flawed. A כרת prohibition is stronger because it applies to every Jew, so the child should be flawed all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one ('how much more so')
A widow married to a כהן גדול, which is forbidden
Her prohibition applies equally to everyone
Isn't it logical?

phrases.english: From a kal vachomer from a widow:
Just as a widow with a High Priest,
whose prohibition does not apply equally to all,
phrases.notes: Only a כהן גדול is forbidden to marry a widow. Everyone else may.

phrases.english: her son is flawed,
this one, whose prohibition applies equally to all,
isn't it logical that her son is flawed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling in Steps 17 and 19.
steps.raayaObject: A child of a union forbidden under כרת is פגום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from a widow with a כהן גדול, whose child is a חלל.

steps.title: The expected objection: a widow becomes disqualified herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the expected objection again. A widow is different because she herself becomes a חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: a widow is different, because she herself becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same objection that stopped the old version in Step 16. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that the widow is a stricter case in one way: the act disqualifies her as well. So maybe her child is flawed only because she is. If that is true, the קל וחומר does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (bringing up an expected objection)
What about X? Since X is different (the standard way to break a קל וחומר)
Becomes a חללה, disqualified from marrying a כהן

phrases.english: And if you will say:
What about a widow?
She is different, since she herself becomes disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings back the objection of Step 16 against the new קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from a widow in Step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widow herself becomes disqualified, so maybe that is why her child is flawed. A woman forbidden under כרת might not share that feature.

steps.title: Here too, his act makes her a זונה
steps.stepSummary: The objection fails here, because relations with a woman forbidden under כרת make her a זונה. So she is disqualified too, just like the widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, once he had relations with her, he made her a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The woman in this case also becomes disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who has forbidden relations of this kind becomes a זונה, and a זונה may not marry a כהן. So the feature that made the widow special exists here too, and the קל וחומר stands. This is exactly why the statement was reworded to be about כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman forbidden to a כהן because of a forbidden union
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: The reworded statement works because a כרת union makes the woman a זונה. So the widow objection that defeated the old version no longer applies, and the child is פגום even according to רבי יהושע.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why the גמרא moved the statement to the case of כרת. That is the case where the widow comparison holds up.

phrases.english: Here too,
once he had relations with her, he made her a zonah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן שֶׁבְּעָלָהּ, עֲשָׂאָהּ זוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the feature which seemed to make the widow different is present here too.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the widow becomes disqualified herself, so the קל וחומר fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The woman forbidden under כרת becomes a זונה through the act, so the קל וחומר holds.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the child of an עבד or גוי with a בת ישראל is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A new statement: everyone agrees that if an עבד or a גוי has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that when a slave or a gentile has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the status of children born to a Jewish woman from an עבד or a גוי. רבי יוחנן says the child is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ruling is ממזר, not just פגום. Again it says 'everyone agrees', so it seems to include sages who usually limit ממזרות to stricter unions. That sets up the discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish slave
A non-Jew
A Jewish woman

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
All agree about a slave or a gentile
who has relations with a Jewish woman
that the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about other children born from forbidden unions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that the child of an עבד or גוי with a בת ישראל is a ממזר.

steps.title: Whose opinion does 'everyone agrees' include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the phrase 'הכל מודים' is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is meant by 'everyone agrees'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on the words 'everyone agrees' from the previous statement. It asks which person's agreement is worth pointing out. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'everyone agrees' suggests that someone might have been expected to disagree. The גמרא wants to know who that surprising person is.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?
Everyone agrees. This is said when even a person you would expect to argue goes along with the ruling.

phrases.english: Who is included by 'everyone agrees'?
phrases.notes: This points back to step 23: everyone agrees that the child of an עבד or a גוי with a Jewish woman is a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question about the wording 'הכל מודים' in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion, one we might expect to disagree, is included in 'everyone agrees'.

steps.title: It includes שמעון התימני, even though he limits which unions produce a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The phrase includes שמעון התימני. He says a ממזר does not come from חייבי לאוין, but his rule applies only in a limited case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is שמעון התימני. Even though שמעון התימני said there is no ממזר from relations forbidden by a plain prohibition, that applies only...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'everyone' includes שמעון התימני. It then starts to explain why his usual view does not apply here. The sentence is cut off and finishes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון התימני holds that relations forbidden only by a לאו do not produce a ממזר. We might have thought he would say the same about an עבד or a גוי. The words 'הני מילי' (that applies only) signal that his rule has a limit, and the גמרא is about to explain why this case falls outside it.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though.
Relationships forbidden by a plain prohibition (לאו), without the punishment of כרת.
This applies only... It introduces a limit on a rule.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמעון התימני is changing his mind. His rule about לאוין stays in place. The גמרא is only showing that this case is different from what his rule covers.

phrases.english: It is Shimon HaTimni.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר שִׁמְעוֹן הַתִּימְנִי
phrases.english: For even though Shimon HaTimni said
there is no mamzer from relations forbidden by a prohibition
that applies only

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְעוֹן הַתִּימְנִי דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24 and begins to explain why שמעון התימני agrees.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'everyone agrees' includes שמעון התימני. The גמרא begins to limit his rule that a ממזר does not come from חייבי לאוין, and the limit is spelled out in the next section.
